recipes.name: Snappy Green Beans
ingredients_raw: 1 (15 ounce) can cut green beans, drained

steps.text: Place bacon in a large, deep skillet. Cook over medium high heat until evenly brown. Drain, crumble and set aside.
Saute onions in bacon grease; add vinegar, and saute until onions are tender. Add green beans and cook until heated through. Crumble the bacon on top.

raw_recipe.headline: Snappy Green Beans
raw_recipe.description: Green beans sauteed with onions and vinegar, topped with crumbled bacon.

review.reviewBody: I could eat this all day, but definitely use fresh, steamed green beans and red wine vinegar.

There's just something about this recipe. The first time I made it, it was on the strength of reviews, but I was hesitant. I've never liked vinegar, and I'm challenged to like much of anything with vinegar in it. Once I made it, I fell in love with it. There's something about the flavor that keeps calling me back to it. It's also one of those recipes that tastes even better the second day as leftovers as the flavors blend. I use red wine vinegar when I make it, that I think adds a little something. I also dump the whole can in, liquid and all, and then cook it down until the liquid is almost all gone to give the beans a Southern style softness. Hauntingly good.

2.27.17 It doesn't take a whole lot to turn ordinary beans into extraordinary beans by adding bacon, onion & vinegar, and I've been making green beans like this for many, many years. I agree with others that you need another type of vinegar with more "snap" (hey, it's in the recipe's name). Would recommend you use cider vinegar or red wine vinegar as opposed to milder white. I did steam my fresh beans in the microwave for about 1 minute 45 seconds to reach that crisp texture that we like rather than using canned beans. Enjoyed, as always!

My husband really liked these, but I made them into a "cold" dish. I used fresh green beans, "garlic red wine vinegar" and also added minced garlic. I also used already cooked bacon to eliminate some fat and then steamed everything together in my microwave, let it cool & served. Nice easy side, thanks Casey.

My mom made these regularly when we were growing up and they were one of the few ways I would eat veggies as a kid. I still love them today. My suggestions for tweaks would be to use tarragon vinegar instead of distilled white and frozen french cut green beans instead of canned. Then it would be perfect like hers :) I'm planning to make a healthier version of this tonight using turkey bacon & EVOO to saute the onions, and my suggestions for tarragon vinegar and frozen french cut beans. Overall though, this is one of my favorite veggie side dishes.

Tasty & healthy- if you make it my way! Saute' onions in a little olive oil. ( I only used half the amount.) Add vinegar, then green beans. Next add 6 T. bacon bits. Heat through- not greasy at all this way. It's tart with the vinegar- we liked it!

fabulous! i cooked the bacon in a skillet sprayed with pam, blotted it between paper towels, wiped out the skillet before sauteing the onions. presto. no grease! and we used balsamic vinegar for a tangy kick. this is a new favorite!

I made mine with fresh green beans, red wine vinegar, bacon with just a little grease (just enough to barely cover the bottom of the skillet), onion and fresh minced garlic. I needed to add a little water about half way thru to finish cooking the beans, but OH BABY was it good when it was done! I only gave it 4 stars because it was amazing with changes... as written, it's 4 stars, how I made it it's 5 stars!

Our family loved this recipe--used one lb. package of Trader Joe's frozen haricot verts, steamed. Cut up six slices of pre-cooked bacon and sauteed with one chopped onion in a little olive oil then added red wine vinegar, kosher salt, freshly ground pepper and the beans. Very little effort for a new and delicious taste.

Wonderful!!! Used frozen green beans, real bacon bits and cider vinegar. Sauted onion (about 1/2 cup) in 1 T heart-healthy margarine. Added cooked green beans, vinegar and bacon bits ans sauted about 10 minutes. Fabulous!!!

Excellent! The only thing I did differently was to add some slivered almonds to the mix. I also used fresh beans out of our garden. I'm making it again tonight and skipping the bacon. Although it was good I don't think the beans needed them. I'm going to saute the onions in a little margarine and use seasoned salt for flavoring. I'll still add in the almonds because the extra crunch is great. Such a nice alternative to boring boiled beans.

These were tangy. It wasn't overpowering, but the vinegar was present. I used frozen green beans and steamed them in the microwave according to package directions. My husband didn't care for these at all. I ate a couple of bites, but it seemed like it needed something more. Perhaps we are simply used to the long simmered southern style green beans and this was not that. They weren't bad, but not really suited to our personal tastes.
This was a big hit even with the kids!
Used 3 slices thick cut. Agree fresh green beans would taste better. Option: add a small amount of sugar; would make this an old German dish my gran always made for us.
As is this recipe is terrible. Canned green beans are not good plus white vinegar makes them too sour.
My husband and I love the flavor. I use 2 cans of green beans instead of one.
These were pretty good. Next time I will cut down on the vinegar, I thought it was too much.
not favored at our house, better described as "sour" green beans than snappy ... may have been better with 6 slices of bacon - I only used 2 (w/ my usual method, more than enough bacon flavor).
Will not be making again. I used red wine vinegar and that was a mistake, causes the onions to turn pink. Flavor is not good either.

I made this with home grown green beans, right off the plant. They were fantastic! All around winner. I've made them a few times. Only thing I don't like is every time they've come out a little greasy. But not enough to deter people to try it.
